A.reason: Feeding real loss reasons into a same-length revision behind a both-order verifier gate is a sound, buildable loop, and the no-reasons control isolates the effect, though it costs about 25% more to run and acceptance rates may be low.

B.reason: Making the finals judge use the benchmark's own card format and rubric, with a mixed panel judging both orders, directly closes the gap between what the system optimises and what raters score; it is a two-day change that can be tested offline by re-judging past finalists.

C.reason: Raters see only the cards, so an editor plus a deterministic checker cheaply removes presentation weaknesses, and the effect can be tested cleanly by re-rating only the edited cards; the gain is capped if idea quality, not presentation, is the real gap.

D.reason: A cheap offline-testable change to the scoring module, but its gain depends on the benchmark rewarding best-of-3 rather than per-card or mean quality, and diversifying can lower the latter by construction.

E.reason: Focusing help on ideas near the top-3 cutoff is well motivated, but multi-cycle mutation adds 30-50% cost and complexity, and mutants overfitting the in-loop judge is a serious risk.

F.reason: It depends on a claim ledger that may not exist, roughly doubles development tokens, takes up to two weeks, and its primary outcome, falsified-claim rate, is not the benchmark's win rate against the baseline.

G.reason: Replacing prose critique with sandbox-checked claims is a heavy redesign that says little on qualitative briefs, and its test measures falsification rate more than rater preference.

H.reason: Selecting from a strict superset of the baseline's candidates puts a floor under outcomes and makes the gain from multi-agent exploration directly visible as a displacement rate, though the output may often just tie the baseline and it adds the cost of a full single-agent run.

I.reason: Weighting judges by reliability and correcting their biases against external verdicts is principled and adds no tokens at equal budget, but it needs about 300 externally rated votes, which may not exist yet, and its parameters go stale when judge models change.

J.reason: A learned correction on top of internal selection, which shrinks back to today's ranking when labels are few, is careful, but it needs 15 or more labelled briefs and a one-off labelling pass that doubles panel cost, and heterogeneity across briefs may swamp the signal.

K.reason: It depends on a mutation contest loop that may not exist, needs about 50 briefs to detect a small effect, and its primary metric, child-beats-parent rate, only indirectly affects benchmark wins.
